title: Hyperlane tile art
description: Hyperlane tiles now show their lanes: each lane is a flat double line (ink outline around a channel in the tile colour) between the midpoints of the hex edges it joins, straight through the centre for opposite edges and bent round it for edges two apart. A ring cap sits on every edge a lane reaches; it half-overlaps the neighbouring tile, so where two hyperlane tiles meet and both have a lane end the two halves close into one ring. The tile is muted indigo with a dotted inner frame, has no planets, and names itself ("Hyperlane connecting edges 2-5", edges counted from 1). Lane data is draw-only; no game logic changed. The same art is used in the map picker's board and thumbnails and in the system inspector.

shots.heading: All 18 tile faces
shots.caption: 83a to 91b at rotation 0, as they come out of the box (A face on the left of each pair). Edge pairs per tile: 83a 2-5, 84a 3-6, 85a/86a 2-6, 87a 1-3 3-5 3-6, 88a 1-5 2-5 3-5, 89a 1-3 1-5 3-5, 90a 2-6 3-5, 91a 1-4 1-5 2-4 and the B faces.

shots.heading: All faces, phone
shots.caption: Same board at 390x844: the lanes are still readable at about 30 px per hex.

shots.heading: Turned copies
shots.caption: 83b, 88a and 90a at 0, 60, 120, 180, 240 and 300 degrees (ids 83b, 83b60 ... 83b300). Every turn moves each lane end one edge on.

shots.heading: Full map, desktop
shots.caption: The real Learn to Play (PoK) layout: hyperlanes (#83a to #88a) beside the gravity rift (#41), nebula (#68) and supernova (#80), with planets, ships and tokens on the other systems. Lane ends line up across neighbouring hyperlane tiles.

shots.heading: Small hexes, desktop
shots.caption: Zoomed out: the double line and the end rings still tell a hyperlane from every system.

shots.heading: Zoomed in
shots.caption: Large hexes: lanes clear of the system number, units and anomaly art.

shots.heading: System inspector
shots.caption: Selecting #88a shows a diagram of its lanes with the text "Hyperlane connecting edges 1-5, 2-5 and 3-5".

shots.heading: Map picker, desktop
shots.caption: Race for Mecatol: the strip's thumbnail and the large preview both draw the lanes; the preview names each lane tile in its tooltip instead of printing its id over the lane.

notes.title: Edge numbering
notes.text: Edges are numbered 1-6 in the order of the engine's ring (south-west, south-east, east, north-east, north-west, west). A unit test checks this against every real community map: wherever two hyperlane tiles touch, a lane end on one side always meets a lane end on the other.

notes.title: Not modelled
notes.text: The engine still treats a hyperlane as an empty hex a ship may pass through; the lane data is only used to draw.
